title: Runtime 1.19 (Draft) — Mixed-workload scheduler (feature flag, default OFF)
author: Connor O'Brien
body:
## Summary
Runtime 1.19 introduces an **experimental mixed-workload scheduler prototype** designed to reduce tail latency (p95/p99) for short/interactive requests when they are co-scheduled with long-context (prefill-heavy) requests.

This capability is **behind a feature flag** and remains **default OFF** for all environments. No customer-facing API behavior changes are expected; changes are limited to request queueing/dispatch and additional observability.

## Why this exists
In mixed prompt-length traffic patterns (e.g., chat + long-context summarization/ingestion), FIFO-like scheduling can allow long-prefill requests to dominate GPU time and inflate wait time for short requests, disproportionately impacting p95/p99.

The prototype scheduler classifies requests into two classes:
- **SHORT**: latency-sensitive, typically smaller prompts / lower predicted prefill cost
- **LONG**: throughput-heavy, typically long prompts / higher predicted prefill cost

It prioritizes SHORT while enforcing **fairness bounds** so LONG is not starved.

## Default behavior (no action required)
- **Flag state:** OFF by default
- **Scheduling policy:** unchanged from 1.18 behavior
- **Metrics/logging:** the new mixed-workload scheduler metrics are emitted only when the policy is enabled (see below); some baseline scheduler metrics remain unchanged.

## Who should care
- **Dedicated / Reserved capacity operators** running mixed chat + long-context workloads.
- **SREs** monitoring tail latency and queue buildup during bursty traffic.
- **Runtime on-call** responding to “p95 spike during long-prompt windows” style escalations.

## Operator-visible changes (when enabled)
When the feature flag is enabled, operators may observe:
1) **Latency distribution shift**
   - Lower p95/p99 for SHORT-class requests under mixed workloads
   - Potentially higher wait time for LONG-class requests under high SHORT load (bounded by fairness settings)

2) **Different queue depth profiles**
   - Separate queue depth signals for SHORT vs LONG (see metrics)
   - Under overload, admission control may activate earlier for LONG depending on config

3) **Additional scheduler logs (sampled)**
   - Sampled structured logs include the chosen class, policy decision, and fairness counters (see “Logging” below)

4) **Small throughput impact is possible**
   - Under some scenarios, we have observed small throughput deltas due to stricter prioritization and fairness guardrails.
   - Treat as experimental until validated against your trace distribution.

## Feature flag and configuration
### Flag name
- **Config key:** `scheduler.mixed_workload.enabled`
- **Default:** `false`

### Core knobs (initial prototype)
These defaults are conservative; avoid tuning during initial canary unless instructed by the runtime scheduling team.

| Config key | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `scheduler.mixed_workload.enabled` | bool | `false` | Enables mixed-workload policy |
| `scheduler.mixed_workload.classifier.long_prompt_tokens` | int | `2048` | Requests with prompt tokens >= threshold are classified LONG (unless overridden by predicted prefill cost) |
| `scheduler.mixed_workload.classifier.prefill_ms_threshold` | int | `35` | If predicted prefill >= threshold, classify LONG |
| `scheduler.mixed_workload.fairness.max_short_burst_ms` | int | `25` | Max continuous SHORT servicing window before forcing LONG service opportunity |
| `scheduler.mixed_workload.fairness.force_long_every_n_dispatches` | int | `32` | Hard guardrail to ensure LONG gets scheduled periodically |
| `scheduler.mixed_workload.backpressure.long_queue_max_depth` | int | `0` (disabled) | Optional cap for LONG queue depth (admission control) |
| `scheduler.mixed_workload.backpressure.short_queue_max_depth` | int | `0` (disabled) | Optional cap for SHORT queue depth (admission control) |

### Example config snippet
(Exact placement depends on environment; shown as a representative runtime config block.)

```yaml
scheduler:
  mixed_workload:
    enabled: true
    classifier:
      long_prompt_tokens: 2048
      prefill_ms_threshold: 35
    fairness:
      max_short_burst_ms: 25
      force_long_every_n_dispatches: 32
    backpressure:
      short_queue_max_depth: 0
      long_queue_max_depth: 0
```

## Observability
### Metrics (emitted when enabled)
The following metrics are added/expanded when the mixed-workload scheduler is enabled:

- Queue depth:
  - `runtime_scheduler_queue_depth{class="short"}`
  - `runtime_scheduler_queue_depth{class="long"}`

- Wait time histograms:
  - `runtime_scheduler_wait_seconds_bucket{class="short"}`
  - `runtime_scheduler_wait_seconds_bucket{class="long"}`

- Service time breakdown (prefill/decode attribution where available):
  - `runtime_scheduler_service_seconds_bucket{phase="prefill",class="short|long"}`
  - `runtime_scheduler_service_seconds_bucket{phase="decode",class="short|long"}`

- Fairness/starvation guardrails:
  - `runtime_scheduler_starvation_events_total{class="long"}`
  - `runtime_scheduler_forced_long_dispatch_total`

### Tracing
When enabled, request traces include spans:
- `scheduler.enqueue`
- `scheduler.dequeue`
- `scheduler.dispatch_decision` (includes class + guardrail decisions)

### Logging (sampled)
Sampled structured logs add fields such as:
- `scheduler_policy=mixed_workload_v0`
- `request_class=short|long`
- `classifier_reason=prompt_tokens|predicted_prefill|fallback`
- `forced_long=true|false`

### Dashboards
See: **Mixed-workload scheduler dashboards** (linked under Related pages). Operators should pin:
- SHORT vs LONG queue depth
- SHORT p95 latency + queue wait component
- LONG starvation events
- Overall throughput / GPU utilization during the canary window

## Rollout guidance (recommended)
This is an experimental feature. Use a staged rollout with explicit rollback criteria.

1) **Perf-canary first**
   - Enable flag for a canary job comparing baseline vs enabled
   - Validate p95 improvement for SHORT without unacceptable LONG impact

2) **Limited production slice (Dedicated only unless approved)**
   - Start at a small percentage of pods/replicas and/or a limited route
   - Maintain the ability to roll back quickly by toggling the flag

3) **Rollback triggers (initial suggestion; refine per service SLOs)**
   - SHORT p95 regresses vs baseline for >10 minutes in steady traffic
   - LONG starvation events become sustained (not single spikes)
   - Queue depth grows without recovery (sign of overload/oscillation)
   - Error rate increase attributable to timeouts/backpressure

For detailed rollout checklist and thresholds, follow SRE guidance in the linked Tail Breakdown page.

## Compatibility and safety notes
- No API changes; request/response formats are unchanged.
- Classification is heuristic; misclassification can occur, especially with unusual prompt distributions.
- The scheduler is designed to avoid LONG starvation via fairness constraints, but tuning parameters can weaken guarantees. Do not tune without coordination.
- Under severe overload, admission control/backpressure behavior may change perceived latency characteristics (e.g., earlier rejection rather than long queueing).

## Known limitations (prototype)
- The classifier uses prompt tokens and predicted prefill cost; it may be less accurate for prompts with atypical token-to-prefill behavior.
- Workloads with many “medium” prompts near the threshold can cause class flapping; if observed, capture traces and contact the scheduling team.
- Throughput impacts are workload-dependent; do not generalize results from one model/SKU to another without re-running the mixed-workload benchmark suite.

## Support / escalation
- Runtime scheduling owners: Sofia Ivanova, Lena Fischer, Marcus Reed
- Perf program: Jonas Weber (benchmarking expectations)
- SRE/SLO review: Sean Gallagher

When filing issues, include:
- Canary window and environment
- Model + GPU SKU
- Prompt length distribution (if known)
- Dashboard screenshots for SHORT/LONG queue depth and wait time
- A small trace sample showing `scheduler.dispatch_decision` spans
